title: Seisho Bypass fully reopened after Typhoon 27 high-wave closures
summary: Resolved na ang Seisho Bypass disruption tracked by ALAM. MLIT and NEXCO Central Japan issued a fifth report and a final report on October 7: several sections reopened at 9:30 a.m., then the remaining downbound closures were lifted at noon after authorities confirmed safe vehicle passage.
why_it_matters: If you were avoiding the Shonan–Odawara coastal corridor because of yesterday's high-wave closures, the specific Seisho Bypass restrictions in this story are no longer in force. Earlier closure maps and rerouting guidance for this incident are now stale.

claims.text: MLIT and NEXCO Central Japan issued a fifth report and a final report on October 7, and NEXCO Central Japan states that all Typhoon 27-related Seisho Bypass closures covered by the notices have been lifted.
claims.basis: Official MLIT/Yokohama National Highway Office release index and NEXCO Central Japan Typhoon 27 notice summary.

claims.text: The fifth report records a partial reopening at 9:30 a.m. on October 7; the final report records the end of the remaining closure at noon.
The earlier ALAM closure map and rerouting advice are now obsolete for this specific incident.
claims.basis: All tracked Seisho Bypass restrictions were officially lifted.

claims.text: Do not assume that every nearby coastal road is unaffected or that future high-wave conditions cannot trigger new restrictions.
claims.basis: The final notice resolves this specific closure event only.

change_summary.previous: The fourth report had expanded the closure, adding an upbound Oiso-nishi IC to Seisho-Ninomiya IC restriction while downbound and toll-road sections remained closed.
change_summary.now: Authorities partially reopened affected sections at 9:30 a.m. October 7 and lifted the remaining Seisho Bypass closure at noon. NEXCO Central Japan now states that all Typhoon 27-related closures covered by these notices have been解除.
change_summary.why_change_matters: This changes the story from active transport disruption to resolved. Drivers should no longer rely on the earlier closure map for this incident.

content.whats_new: Resolved na: the Seisho Bypass restrictions tracked in this story were fully lifted by noon on October 7 after safety checks.
content.skeptical_view: A final reopening notice closes this specific road event; it does not prove that all coastal infrastructure in Kanagawa is unaffected or eliminate the possibility of new weather-related restrictions.
content.what_next: Normal trip planning can resume for this specific closure, but check live road and weather information before coastal travel because conditions can change.
content.what_would_change_mind: A new official restriction or another high-wave closure affecting the same corridor would constitute a new material development.
content.recommendation: If you rerouted because of this incident, puwede nang alisin ang Seisho-specific closure assumption from your route plan. Still check live traffic before departure.
